summary: Frontend-only E2E validation (mobile 390x844, public URL) of the 3 'Il Tuo Laboratorio' improvements: (1) LabTour non-blocking overlay, (2) DayClose Step-3 digital signature embedded in the closure PDF, (3) persisted default supplier email in Magazzino + low-stock quick order. Plus DayClose regression (wizard/storico, 3 steps, nav, language switcher). ALL scenarios PASSED with no console errors. Verified server-side that the signature is stored (base64, 7758 chars) and that the generated PDF contains an embedded /Subtype /Image XObject (signature) with 200/application/pdf.

issues: A thin decorative colour strip (green/black/red/yellow bars) is visible above the sticky header at the very top edge of the viewport on 390px width – looks like a background image bleeding through; purely cosmetic.

action_items: No blocking action needed for the 3 requested features.
Optional: silence the pre-login 401 on the session/me call (logged as a console error before authentication) to keep the console clean.
Optional cosmetic: check the colour strip bleeding above the header on mobile widths.
critical_code_review_comments: LabTour: the document-level click listener calls finish() on ANY outside-card click, including clicks on non-interactive background – acceptable UX, but note the tour is then permanently marked seen (storageKey written) even on an accidental tap. Consider only persisting after the user reaches the last step or skips explicitly.
DayClose.jsx is 523 lines and mixes wizard, inventory, storico and SignaturePad – consider extracting SignaturePad and the Magazzino card into separate components.

SignaturePad: onChange only fires on pointer-up (end). If the user drags out of the canvas and releases outside, onPointerLeave covers it – OK, but the canvas is not scaled to devicePixelRatio, so the stored PNG is fixed 600x180 (fine for PDF).
supplierOrder() falls back to a hardcoded SUPPLIERS email when the saved field is empty – acceptable, but no email format validation on supplier-email input before building the mailto.

success_rate.backend: not tested (frontend-only request); PDF endpoint spot-checked 200/application/pdf

seed_data_creation: Created 1 day_closure (lot ML-20260826-74) with signature for admin@mikilab.de and a transient inventory row TEST_Farina0. Both cleaned up: day_closures deleted (1), haccp_logs 0 (none created since no temps/cleaning were filled), TEST_ inventory items 0 remaining. admin now has 0 closures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Detailed results: (1) LabTour: after localStorage.removeItem('mikilab_lab_tour_v1') + reload, lab-tour count=1 on nav-tab-maestro; clicking capo-quicklink-dayclose directly (no tour buttons) opened dayclose (count=1) AND dismissed the tour (lab-tour count=0) – overlay does NOT swallow the tap. (2) Signature: mouse drag on signature-pad painted 1573 non-transparent pixels, placeholder 'Firma qui' disappeared; signature-clear reset to 0 pixels and restored the placeholder; dayclose-confirm -> dayclose-celebrate -> dayclose-download-pdf triggered a real download (chiusura-ML-20260826-74.pdf, 5644 bytes, %PDF header) with GET /api/day-close/{id}/pdf?lang=it -> 200 application/pdf; Mongo shows signature base64 stored; PDF bytes contain /Subtype /Image confirming embedding. (3) supplier-email typed 'ordini@fornitore.it' -> localStorage mikilab_supplier_email persisted and survived a reload; adding inv item with qty 2 / threshold 10 rendered dayclose-lowstock and dayclose-order-supplier (visible + enabled). (4) Regression: steps 1/2/3 + dayclose-prev all render, storico mode lists the closure and its storico-pdf-<id> download returns 200 application/pdf, back to wizard works; header shows only IT and DE. Only console error observed: a pre-login 401 (auth/me) – benign. Automation tip confirmed: nav-tab-maestro click sometimes needs a retry loop after login.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A – all three fixes verified working. LabTour fix works because the backdrop is pointer-events-none and a document click listener finishes the tour while the click still reaches the underlying tool tile.
